documented_counties.evidence: UT Plant Resources Center Natural Purola flora explicitly lists Diospyros texana in the North Hays County flora; JACQ also preserves Hays County wild seed provenance.
UC Davis Saratoga horticultural report records wild Diospyros texana provenance from Travis County; Travis County BCP monitoring also records it in natural preserve vegetation.
UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County explicitly treats Diospyros texana.

target_zone_range.native_context: Kew treats the species as native from Texas to northeastern Mexico; BONAP has a Texas county-distribution map.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county presence inferred from source-pool membership or iNaturalist counts.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the trunk and leaf underside: smooth pale gray to reddish-gray bark that peels/mottles, plus small thick obovate leaves with a densely hairy lower surface. In fruit, black pubescent berries are highly diagnostic.
morphology.habit: Shrub to small tree, often multi-stemmed; tardily deciduous to semi-evergreen depending on site.
morphology.leaves: Alternate, simple, small (about 2–5 cm in FNA), usually obovate; upper surface dark/glossy, lower surface tomentose.
morphology.reproductive: White urn-shaped flowers; FNA separates it by flowers on previous-season twigs, pubescent ovaries, and black berries that remain pubescent.
morphology.fruit: Black berry about 1.5–2.5 cm, generally 3–8 seeded, with persistent calyx.

confusers.separator: FNA key: D. texana has much smaller 2–5 cm leaves with tomentose lower surfaces, flowers on previous-season twigs, pubescent ovaries, and pubescent black fruit; D. virginiana usually has 6–15 cm leaves, current-season flowers and glabrous yellow-orange to dark-red fruit.

photo_verification.note: USFS FEIS provides credited CC BY-NC field images for habit and leaf/unripe fruit; Texas A&M Rangelands provides a slideshow; iNaturalist guide material and Central Texas photo sources provide flower/fruit coverage.
